title: Numbers, Booleans & Erlang's Comparison Operators

mentalModelCheck.question: What is the evaluated result of the Erlang expression (10 =:= 10.0) orelse (5 <= 10)?

options.label: true, because 10 equals 10.0 and 5 is less than or equal to 10
options.explanation: 10 =:= 10.0 evaluates to false because an integer and float are different types, and <= is a compiler syntax error!

options.label: A compiler syntax error, because less-than-or-equal must be written as =< in Erlang
options.explanation: <= is reserved for binary comprehensions. Less-than-or-equal must be written =<.

options.label: false, because both sides evaluate to false
options.explanation: The code never evaluates to false because <= fails to compile.
